summary: Steuben County International Derrick tower built 1940-41 by a CCC camp; staffed 1943-1972; sold 1979. All four lists say removed or gone.

facts.design: International Derrick tower, 82 ft 6 in; Starr's list gives a 1937 International Derrick model
facts.status_note: Removed and sold in 1979, per the nysffla.org list; no source read describes the site now.
facts.agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation

events.note: Erected by CCC Camp S-123 at Beaver Dams. The nysffla.org list says the work began in 1940 and was completed in 1941; Starr's list gives 1940 as the opening year.
First staffed in 1943, when it reported 65 fires and 90 visitors.
Staffed regularly until 1972, when aerial detection led to the tower being closed.
Closed and placed on the inactive list.
Maintained for flood emergency communications until 1978.
Declared excess, no longer needed for fire or flood emergencies, and sold.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Starr's list gives 1940 as the opening year. The nysffla.org list says CCC work began in 1940 and was completed in 1941. The story gives both dates.

notes_for_editor: Four lists agree the tower is gone or removed: nysffla.org, Starr's 2011 list, CNY Hiking and the Forest Fire Lookout Association. The history (build, staffing, 1972 closure, 1978 flood use, 1979 sale) comes from the nysffla.org entry alone; Starr's list corroborates the 1940 opening, the 1937 model and the seasonal operation. The build dates differ slightly: 1940 opened (Starr) and 1940 to 1941 (nysffla.org). The story gives both. The link between the nysffla.org entry and Erwin Mountain rests on the 4 miles west of Corning location, the Steuben County placement and the 1,710 ft elevation in Starr and CNY Hiking; the brief's name Erwin Mountain matches the FFLOS listing; the nysffla.org list calls it Erwin Fire Tower and Starr calls it Erwin Mtn. The tower's height is recorded as the 82 ft 6 in tower dimension, with no cab-floor height, so no height_m is given. No source describes the Game Management Area site today. No photos recorded.
